recipes.name: Leftover Chicken Croquettes
ingredients_raw: 3 cups cooked, finely chopped chicken meat

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Combine chicken, bread crumbs, and two eggs in a large bowl; stir in onion until well combined. If mixture is too dry to form patties, mix in remaining egg. Mix in parsley, salt, and pepper.
Wipe out the skillet; add remaining 1 tablespoon oil and heat over medium heat. Working in batches, fry patties until golden brown and crispy, 4 to 6 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Leftover Chicken Croquettes
raw_recipe.description: Looking for an easy leftover chicken recipe? These simple chicken croquettes are perfectly seasoned and pan-fried until golden brown and crispy.

review.reviewBody:
This is a good basic recipe. Here is how I tweaked it, and they turned out wonderful! Mince all ingredients to make the patties form well. I also did not add any salt. Saute 1 large onion, 2 large crushed cloves garlic, 1 large red sweet pepper; in 2 TBL grape seed oil. Cool Mix chicken with the bread crumbs. Add the sauted veggies and include: 1TBL basil, 1Tsp cilantro, 1/3 Cup finely grated parmesean cheese, 1-2 tsp habenaro hot sauce, and 1-2 TBL worchestershire sauce. Add 3 eggs slightly beaten. Form small patties and place on cookie
sheet greased with canola oil spray. Bake 12 minutes at 350 degrees. (30 minutes is way too long, will dry them out) Enjoy!

These were FANTASTIC! I read through a lot of reviews before making them and combined some of the ideas. I'll save you the time here... 
 You definitely want to sautee the onions, it makes a big difference. Combine the sauteed onions and leftover chicken in the food processor, it will improve the texture and help the patties stay together. I used savory herb stuffing in place of the bread crumbs. I also added fresh parmesan cheese, oregano, basil, and some garlic powder. My mix was a little dry at this point so I added some chicken stock. 
 Here is the key...Mix all of the ingredients together EXCEPT FOR THE EGG!!! TASTE IT! If it doesn't taste good at this point, it won't taste any better when you cook it:) Season it until it tastes good, then add the eggs. I baked mine on a cookie sheet at 350 until they were golden brown(about 20 minutes). 
 Thanks for a great recipe and thank you to all of the reviewers before me for their tweaks:)

Loved the idea of using leftover chicken, although I tweaked mine according to other's reviews. They turned out delicious! I used 3 cups of leftover chicken, chopped it up. I sauted 2 cups onions with 4 minced garlic cloves and added a medium red pepper. 
I used 1 1/4 cup Italiano breadcrumbs, 1/3 cup finely grated parmesan cheese, 1.5 tbsp worcestershire sauce, 2 eggs, 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, 1/2 tbsp dried basil, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp garlic and pepper spice, 1/2 tsp Mrs. Dash chicken seasoning, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp dried cilantro. Mix them all together and bake in the oven for 15 minutes on 350, turning them over in between. I also pan fried them, but my Husband and I loved them baked! Super delicious and not dry at all! This recipe made about 10 patties !

These were okay and good for a quick meal. What I did, was skipped cooking the onion and used finely diced raw red onion. It added a little more flavor. Then made them into a chicken sandwich. I toasted the bun, layered a slice of tomato and some lettuce and topped it with my own honey mustard sauce. They were good for something quick for dinner.

Very low sodium with adjustments. Yum! Tweaked as follows: Sauteed 2 lg onions, diced, in 2 TBL butter. Added 1.5 cups Panko crumbs, 3 c finely chopped chicken and seasoned with 2 tsp poultry seasoning, generous shakes of celery seed, dill weed and fresh ground black pepper. Tasted good so added 3 eggs, made 17 patties. I baked them at 350 for 23 minutes on a sheet sprayed with Pam. I calculate sodium per patty as 30 mg. Delish as is, gravy would be a bonus

Very good. Made changes based on what I had in the house and other reviews. For the onion: I used 1 cup sauteed yellow onion, 2 thinly sliced scallions, and used some carmelized onion I had in my freezer. Processed about 1 cup of the meat along with the carmelized onion in the food processor. Used herb flavored stuffing in place of bread crumbs. Added some fresh basil, dried oregano, garlic powder and Parmesan cheese. I used 3 eggs but added them last, AFTER I had already tasted the mixture and had it to my liking. Baked at 350* for 20 minutes. Served with Garlic Mayonnaise Aioli from this site (to which I did 1/2 sour cream and 1/2 mayo, used 4 roasted garlic cloves and added smoked paprika). Yummy Dish!

I had leftover chicken from two fast food places, takeout from the local buffet restaurant, and the hot bar at our grocery store, all taking up way too much real estate in my fridge. (Yes, I am that person.) I typed “leftover chicken” and this recipe popped up. I had all the ingredients on hand, including the onion that was in the veggie drawer so long it was sprouting (again, I am that person). I followed the advice of a couple reviewers and blended all the ingredients in my hand chopper except the 3 eggs (I thought 3 would be too many but was not), which I added last, along with a few splashes of chicken broth. The Parmesan cheese is an excellent addition. I baked for 13 minutes at 350. My husband loved them as did I, but he suggested some gravy would make them perfect. I’ll likely make some to go with the remaining patties. Excellent use of leftovers!

I've made this twice now, both times in the oven. The first was pretty basic adding a few spices as directed in the comments. It was good but unimpressive. 
The second time I sauted onions, garlic, sweet pepper and celery. Added a splash of chicken broth along with the 2 eggs and a few left over canned mushroom pieces from the fridge. I added some Italian breadcrumbs that were mixed with parma cheese that I had left over for the dry base along with S&P,parsley, oregano, and basil for spice and mixed it all together topping with a thin slice of garden tomato, some mozzarella and a splash of spaghetti sauce on top. I made it in the morning and put the patties in the fridge till dinner time. Then cooked 30 minutes in the oven at 350. Served over a few egg noodles and it was wonderful!

This tasted very good—a little better than expected. I used many of the tweaks others suggested, such as an extra egg, garlic powder, and baking them. I ended up frying then in a skillet for a couple of minutes to get a little more crunch. They tasted great.

Pretty good base recipe for us. I added more seasonings like garlic, cayenne, celery, Worcestershire, parmesan, basil. But I was using plain panko crumbs so was trying to make up for flavor and add some additional at the same time. Mixed it all up and let it sit for about thirty minutes before frying. Hubbs liked it and I liked using up leftovers, so a great recipe for that! Will remember this in the future because it was so simple and have the ingredients on hand, or just sub for whatever you have.

I used this as a "starter" recipe. My food processor got a work out ! I ground my leftover chicken and ground the onions in the food processor before sauteing them. Ground up a stalk of celery fairly finely and used packaged seasoned stuffing mix and ground it up in the food processor as well. As others have suggested, doing this makes for a more uniform consistency and makes it easier for the patties to stay together. I had to use dried parsley as I didn't have any fresh. I added garlic, a little oregano and a pinch of cayenne. I didn't really measure how much chicken, onion and stuffing mix I used, just dumped it all in a bowl once it was all ground up. 2 eggs left it a little dry, so I added a splash of home made chicken stock. This time, I fried them in a little oil in a non-stick skillet, but next time will try baking them in the oven as others have suggested. They were quite good fried, but I think baking them might be a nice option. I had mine plain, but my hubby had his with some leftover white gravy with a hefty dose of coarse ground black pepper. Both were good! Thank you for a great "starter" recipe for chicken croquettes!

Pretty good, but I bumped them up a little. I added red peppers, and a little bit of crumbled bacon. I served them with sour cream, Sriracha and avocado. It was a decent way to make breakfast with last night's chicken.
This recipe is awesome. I did add red pepper flakes & garlic powder to it. It was delicious.
Used Italian flavored bread crumbs Used air fryer, but patties stuck to “nonstick “tray with Pam. Making today Frying in cast iron pan with oil

I minced a medium onion and 1/2 bell pepper and then sautéed in small amount of butter. Very finely chopped the chicken. Added onion and garlic powder as well. Used 3 eggs and 1 cup of bread crumbs. Made patties earlier and refrigerated them for a couple hours. Baked for 15 minutes at 350 then another 10 at 375 . Didn’t dry out. Will make a gravy next time . Served with Chef Johns Air Fryer French Fries.
Good basic recipe. Should have read reviews. Very dry even with 3 eggs. Added chicken broth. Will tweak with red peppers. Made a gravy with stock/butter/flour

I made it just like the recipe stated with 2 eggs. Hubby has difficulty swallowing a lot of meats. I purchased 1 pound of rotisserie chicken & put it in the food processor for a second or 2. (1.5 cups of the chicken = 12 oz.) I made 8 patties that were 3 oz each & a spare that was 2 oz. When hubby saw what was for supper he split his pattie and put a slice of lite cheese on each half & microwaved it. It was successful since he had no swallowing problems & he requested a pattie be moved from the freezer so he could have it tomorrow. Next time I'll add a bit more moisture to them mix.
Thank you for providing the framework for a good recipe. We can add/subtract whatever we want!
Added garlic powder and some wochestershire for a bit more zip.
Nothing special, not very tasty. Won't be making it again.
